results.evidence: I loaded the schema through importlib.resources.files('cottonwood') and it passed Draft202012Validator.check_schema. The valid record had type, organization.name, verified_facts, hypothesis and one evidence item with url, observed_at and excerpt, and it produced no errors. Removing each of type, organization.name, verified_facts, hypothesis, evidence, evidence[0].url and evidence[0].observed_at gave a 'required' error. For organization.name the error path is ['organization'] and for evidence[0].url and observed_at it is ['evidence', 0]. That is the parent object, and the message names the missing field. An evidence item with neither excerpt nor observation is rejected through anyOf (error path ['evidence', 0]). The 47 tests in tests/test_prospects_validate.py passed.

tests/test_prospects_validate.py has a parametrized test_field_rules (lines 126-145) that calls validate_record with TODAY=2026-11-30 and record number 2. It asserts the exact line 'rejected record 2: <field>: <rule>' for every case in the AC: type 'prospect' (type: enum), empty evidence (evidence: minItems), 'ftp://acme.com/x' and 'https://' (evidence[0].url: url), '2026-02-30' (date), '2026-12-01' (not-future), 'not-an-email' (contact.email: email) and 'call me' (contact.phone: phone). test_record_id_is_shown_in_the_prefix asserts 'rejected record 2 (acme-1): type: enum'. test_observed_today_is_accepted checks that observed_at '2026-11-30' returns a ProspectRecord. Rejection.line() in cottonwood/validate.py builds f"rejected {self.label()}: {self.field}: {self.rule}". I ran the suite with uv and 47 tests passed. My own standalone probe could not run in this sandbox, so the verdict rests on the repo tests, which assert the exact strings.

Tests in tests/test_prospects_validate.py cover every case in the AC, and the 14 value/amount/basis tests passed. They check that 250000.00 with founder-estimated validates and keeps the text '250000.00'. They check that an amount with no basis gives 'value.basis: required'. They check that basis 'guess' gives 'value.basis: enum'. They check that '2.5e5', '-1', 'abc' and '1,000' each give 'value.amount: decimal'. The decimal rule is the regex ^\d+(\.\d+)?$ at validate.py:84, applied at validate.py:385. I did not run the validator directly outside the test suite.

results.evidence: load_records (cottonwood/validate.py:197-215) raises FileError with the path for a wrong extension, a missing file, invalid JSON, and a non-array JSON top level (lines 206, 210, 222, 224). It does the same for a CSV header that lacks a required column such as evidence_url (line 244). CSV rows are numbered from 1 (line 247). _csv_record skips empty cells, and _csv_scalar splits verified_facts on newlines (lines 262-278). tests/test_prospects_validate.py:244-290 loads a two-row CSV and asserts numbers [1, 2] and data equal to the JSON pair. Lines 342-347 check that each of the five error cases raises FileError with the path in the message. All 47 tests in tests/test_prospects_validate.py passed.
